metas.name: Argentina - Architecture - Mar del Plata Architecture
metas.note: In Mar Del Plata and surrounding cities (such as Miramar and Necochea), a unique style of architecture can be found. Its main features include quartzite stoned facades, orange tiled roofs, attached garages, and vault shaped porches.

metas.name: Argentina - Architecture - Red Brick Architecture
metas.note: Red bricks, similar to what is common in Bolivia, can be found in the northwest of the country, especially in western Jujuy.

metas.name: Brazil - Architecture - European Architecture
metas.note: Buildings in the southern states, mainly Santa Catarina, can be of European influence (typically vaguely German) in design and style.

metas.name: Brazil - Architecture - Red Brick Architecture
metas.note: Houses made out of red brick are more common in Northeastern Brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Architecture - Stilt Houses
metas.note: Wooden houses on stilts are very common in the state of Acre.

metas.name: Colombia - Architecture - Guatape
metas.note: Bright Colored Houses & Unique Pavement.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Architecture - Straw/Thatched Roofs
metas.note: Houses with roofs like this are commonly found along the coast, especially near Cartagena and Barranquilla.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: France - Architecture - Alpine Architecture
metas.note:
Alpine architecture, unmistakable for its light coloured base and extensive wooden elements, is unsurprisingly found in the Alps.

NOTE: Similar houses can be found in the touristic parts of Pyrenees.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Basque Architecture
metas.note:
White houses with, often colourful, timber framing are a staple of Basque architecture that extends beyond the Basque speaking area. The timber frame colour (in this case red) will be consistent with other wooden elements, like window shutters and gates.

NOTE: They’re also common in parts of Northern Spain, where the timber frames are usually unpainted.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Belle-Île-en-Mer Architecture
metas.note:
On the Breton island Belle-Île-en-Mer you can find houses typical for Brittany combined with colourful façades and outlines, superficially similar to houses in Portugal.

NOTE: The entire island was only covered with an often oversaturated Generation 2 camera.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Black Shingle Roof
metas.note: Black shingle roofs are primarily found in the northwest, the rough cutoff being the Loire river. Other areas include near the Belgian border, the south-centre, and the Pyrenees, making black roofs a good clue for Alps-Pyrenees toss-ups.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Black Shingle Roofs with Mountains
metas.note: Black shingle roofs are often found in the Pyrenees, making black roofs a good clue for Alps-Pyrenees toss-ups.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Brick House / Black Roof
metas.note:
Found in the North (mostly Belgium border)

Note by MB: Brick Houses also often have Red Roofs. Houses with Black Roofs do not appear around Toulouse (unlike those with red roofs).

What I find more useful to differentiate the roof types is the materials. "Black Roofs" are shingles, while "Red Roofs" are actual tiles (which can also get very dark)
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Architecture - Brick House / Red Rooftiles
metas.note:
Brick roofs with red rooftiles can be found in the North mostly. Sometimes, they're also found around Toulouse.

Note by MB: With red tiles, Toulouse is an option, with black shingles, it isn't. What I find more useful to differentiate the roof types is the materials. "Black Roofs" are shingles, while "Red Roofs" are actual tiles (which can also get very dark)
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Architecture - Brittany Architecture
metas.note: Brittany has one of the most recognizable and consistent architectures in the country. Common elements include, in addition to black roofs, edge chimneys, black slate walls and stones surrounding doors and windows. The walls will be either very light coloured or made of stone.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Germanic Architecture
metas.note:
Many elements of Germanic architecture are concentrated in Alsace, such as timber framing and half-hip roof. Furthermore, roofs with fish scale tiles are more common in this region.

Beware that these elements are sometimes incorporated into architecture in other parts of France, and are most reliable in conjunction with one another.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Ile de France Architecture
metas.note: Walls made of uneven cream coloured to orange stones, glued with mortar and often incorporating red brick details can be found in the towns surrounding Paris. Note that the city of Paris itself generally does not have this architecture.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Mansard Roof
metas.note:
Mansard roofs, also known as French windows, are a very common feature of Parisian architecture. They’re made up of steep black shingle roofs with inserted dormer windows. While not unique to Paris, it is a good clue in abundance and on wide boulevards.

On some occasions, they can also be found in the North of France.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Architecture - Old Toulouse Architecture
metas.note: In and around Toulouse, mainly in old towns, you will commonly find bright orange brick buildings. They differ from brick houses near Belgium by the bricks being brighter, as well as somewhat Mediterranean looking architectural features, such as wooden shutters, being common.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Stone House / Black Shingle Roof
metas.note:
Found in Western France, mainly in Bretagne.

Note by MB: What I find more useful to differentiate the roof types is the materials. "Black Roofs" are shingles, while "Red Roofs" are actual tiles (which can also get very dark)
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Architecture - Stone House / Red Rooftiles
metas.note:
Can be found all over France, but mainly central and southern.

Note by MB: What I find more useful to differentiate the roof types is the materials. "Black Roofs" are shingles, while "Red Roofs" are actual tiles (which can also get very dark)
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Architecture - U-Tiles
metas.note: Roofs in the south of the country will often be made up of rounded tiles overlapping one another, often varying in colour.

metas.name: France - Architecture - West Coast Architecture
metas.note: The houses along the West Coast, from Nantes to Bayonne are usually low, with white walls, and red roofs.
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Arches in Half-Timbered houses
metas.note: This type of half-timbered house with arches at the ground floor is very common in this region of Saxony.

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Commie Blocks
metas.note: These large, utilitarian apartment buildings constructed during the socialist era, that are also known as 'Commie blocks' are common in all of former East Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Fishscale Walls
metas.note: Houses with black slate walls, resembling fish scales, are commonly found in a large area of central Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Frisian Architecture
metas.note: Thatched roofs and rock walls are most common on the North Frisian Islands, as well as mainland Schleswig-Holstein. You can also commonly find them in coastal resort towns in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Red Brick
metas.note:
These brick houses are generally concentrated in northwestern Germany.

NOTE: This map is very approximate.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Andhra Pradesh - Thatched Roofs
metas.note:
Within Andhra Pradesh, thatched roofs can commonly be found in three places.

  • Mainly south east of Guntur
  • Secondarily south of Nellore, where a rare red car can be found.
  • Sparsely around Srikakulam
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Assam - Thatched Roofs
metas.note: Within Assam, you can find thatched roofs all the way north east in the state.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Assam - Woven Walls
metas.note: In Assam, you can find houses with woven walls along the border to Arunachal Pradesh, north of Tinsukia.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Bihar - Tin Hip Roof
metas.note: If you see these hip roofs made out of tin - which are usually found in West Bengal - in Bihar, you're in the Northeastern Quarter of Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Bihar - Wide W Tiles
metas.note:
Within Bihar, you can find regular Wide W Tiles around Katihar.

Reminder: This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Blue Walls & Tiles
metas.note: Houses with tiled roofs and blue painted walls are very common in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, a little less in Madhya Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Brick Kiln
metas.note: In poorer parts of the Ganges Valley it is common for villages to construct their own large chimneys to fire clay into bricks. These can be seen from far away and are a good clue for the Ganges Valley specifically, especially UP and Bihar. Note that they are also fairly common in the poorer eastern parts of Tamil Nadu.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Clay House
metas.note: Houses made out of clay are most common in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand. There's some spill in far southwestern Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Clay House
metas.note: Clay houses exist a lot in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, and some spill can be seen in southwestern Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Clay Huts
metas.note: White painted clay huts are found in northwestern Bihar, northwest of Muzaffapur.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt, India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Colorful Walls
metas.note: Houses with colorful, particularly blue painted walls, can be found in the areas around Eastern Madhya, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Corrugated Hip Roof
metas.note: Large hip roofs made of corrugated sheet metal are found in West Bengal and adjacent areas in Bihar and Odisha.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Dravidian Temple
metas.note:
- Shorter and "pyramidal" towers (Vimana) - most easily recognizable

  • Monumental and ornate gate (Gopuram)
  • Door Guardian Statues (Dvarapala)

Found in the South of India.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Dumka House
metas.note: Houses between Dumka and Pakur have long tiled roofs and walls are painted in two colors (green/blue with an orange/brown color at the bottom
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Elevated Bengali Roof
metas.note:
Found mostly in the main, southern part of West Bengal, but more in the west. Sometimes also found in Bihar at the border to eastern Nepal.

Note by MB: This meta is not sufficiently researched, but it's still good to know
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Flat Gooner (actually Guna) Tiles
metas.note: Flat Guna tiles is just a tiled roof full of staple-shaped tiles. It can be found around Prayagraj, south east of the state.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Flat Tiles
metas.note: Flat tiles seem to be the worst type of tile by their appearance. They are mainly found in Madhya Pradesh and southern Uttar pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Gooner (actually Guna) Tiles
metas.note:
It has a “U” shape but there is a flatter shaped tile connecting tiles to each other.

It’s very common in southeastern Uttar Pradesh, western Bihar and rarely in northeastern Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Green House
metas.note: Houses in Odisha are often painted green.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Hay Hut
metas.note: These huts that are made entirely out of hay, and have thatched roofs are found in Southwestern Bihar, mainly between Patna and Gaya.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Jammu Architecture
metas.note:
Jammu looks like a fairly developed state compared to most places in India. The architecture looks richer and overall way nicer. Punjab has a similar architecture.

50/50 Tip ! It can be hard to differentiate Punjab and Jammu in urban rounds due to the similarity of their architecture. If you see rich looking houses, look at the car to know whether you are in Punjab or in Jammu. If you don’t see one of the two Jammu cars (boxy with top right thread or central strap, see image 3&4), click Punjab.

Note by MB: This 50/50 tip is not 100% reliable, so look at other clues (like Punjabi language) too.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Jharkhand - Wide W Tiles
metas.note: In the eastern parts of Jharkhand, you can find some West Bengal wide W tiles spill
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - Flat Tiles
metas.note: Flat tiles can be spotted in random places in Madhya Pradesh, but mainly around Guna, Chhatarpur and Sagar in the center of the state.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - Slate Roofs
metas.note: Slate roofs in Madhya Pradesh can be found west of Sagar
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - U Tiles
metas.note: U tiles are more common in the eastern half of Madhya Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - W Tiles
metas.note: W tiles are quite rare in Madhya Pradesh but can still be seen west of Jabalpur and south of Guna
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Nalukettu
metas.note: Nallukettu architecture has distinct roofs, which are often very high and red. This style is often found around Kerala Backwaters.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - Thatched Roofs
metas.note:
Thatched roofs can be found pretty much all over the eastern coast of India. In the state of Odisha, they can mostly be seen between Balasore and Puri, but also more inland and in the southwest of the state.

If you see only thatched, the coast is more likely.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - U-Tiles
metas.note: U tiles are commonly found on the northwest of the state, on the borders with Jharkhand and Chhattsgarh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - U-Tiles & Thatched Roofs
metas.note: When mixed with thatched roofs, U Tiles are most commonly found around Umerkote.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - W-Tiles
metas.note:
W tiled roofs can be found in two areas in Odisha:

  • corridor north of Bhubaneswar
  • Southwestern Odisha, southwest of Bhawanipatna
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - W-Tiles & Thatched Roofs
metas.note:
W tiled roofs combined with Thatched Roofs can be found in two areas in Odisha:

  • corridor north of Bhubaneswar
  • Southwestern Odisha, southwest of Bhawanipatna

Note by MB: This is also true if you just see W-Tiles, without Thatched Roofs.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - W-Tiles & U-Tiles
metas.note: When mixed with W-Tiles, U-Tiles are most commonly found around Umerkote.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Orange/Black Wide W Tiles
metas.note:
If you see orange/black wide W tiles, you're probably around Madhubani (BR).

Reminder: This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Plastered Woven Wall
metas.note: Woven walls, plastered with clay are found on the western half of the Bihar-Nepal border.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Red Brick
metas.note: While Red Brick can be found anywhere in India, there is a notable concentration in the Ganges River Valley, especially towards the West.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Shimla Vibes
metas.note:
Shimla is definitely the place in the Himalayas with the biggest amount of bright green and bright red roofs (and architecture in general).

Note by MB: It also spams Himalayan Cedars.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Sikhism
metas.note: Gurdwaras, which can typically be recognised by their white domes and ornate walls, are most common in Punjab. You can also sometimes recognise them by the Sikh Khanda symbol, which represents the religion.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Sikkim Roof
metas.note: Roofs in Sikkim often have this short "curtain" hanging down on the side of the roof.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Architecture - Slate Roof - Karnataka/Telangana
metas.note:
Slate roofs can be found in a very specific area between Kalaburagi and Hyderabad in Telangana.

Note by MB: This is the same area where they use the thin grey stones (see thin grey stones meta), and thus you can often see them in combination
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Square Panel Houses
metas.note: Houses made of square panels separated by thin beams are found in Northeast India, mainly in Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Stick Huts
metas.note: Wooden huts with sticks around can be found in the western half of Bihar, at a latitude between Patna and Muzaffarpur..
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt, India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Tamil Nadu Colors
metas.note: Houses with very "strong colors", such as dark yellow, pink, purple, are often found in Tamil Nadu, and sometimes in Kerala and Andhra Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India GeoGuessr Guide - 2024 Edition by duskden2

metas.name: India - Architecture - Tamil Nadu House
metas.note:
In Tamil Nadu, you will often come across quite good looking houses, the most recognizable are the ones with W tiled roofs and blueish paint. The combination of the color and the tiles should be 95% Tamil Nadu, the remaining 5% being spill in bordering states.

W tiled roofs are pretty much everywhere but somewhat less common in the northeast and on the eastern coast, where U tiles can be found more commonly.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Thatched Hay Roofs
metas.note: Houses or huts with thatched roofs are mainly found along the east coast and northern plains. Large hay mounds are also generally more common in this region. Thatched roofs from Uttar Pradesh to Odisha tend to be made of fine pieces of hay.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Thatched Palm Roofs
metas.note: Houses or huts with thatched roofs are mainly found along the east coast and northern plains. Large hay mounds are also generally more common in this region. Thatched roofs from Odisha to Tamil Nadu tend to be made of dried palm fans.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Thatched Roofs - Tamil Nadu
metas.note: In Tamil Nadu, thatched roofs are more common south east of Thanjavur.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Thin Grey Stones
metas.note: The area on the border of Telangana and Karnataka often have houses with roofs made out of distinctly thin grey bricks. These grey bricks and similar coloured rocks are sometimes also seen in walls and scattered on the ground in stockyards.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Triangle Metal Roofs
metas.note: Metal roofs, with a small triangle near the top, are common in Northeast India.

metas.name: India - Architecture - U-Tiles
metas.note:
These rounded tiles are found mostly in

  • Chhattisgarh
  • Jharkhand
  • Bihar
  • Eastern Madhya

You can also find them in

  • Eastern Gujarat
  • Eastern Tamil Nadu
  • North-Western Telangana
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - U-Tiles - Tamil Nadu
metas.note:
U tiled roofs are quite rare in Tamil Nadu, but if you come across such roofs, it should be in the northeast.

It is possible to find some further down near Thanjavur, but it will more likely come with the combination of thatched roofs.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - W-Tiles
metas.note: W-Tiles are mostly found on the western coast and in Tamil Nadu, but it also goes further inland in western Madhya Pradesh and in Telangana.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - W-Tiles - Karnataka
metas.note: If you come across a W tiled roof in Karnataka, you can basically go in the western/southwestern part
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - W-Tiles - Telangana
metas.note:
The only type of tile in Telangana is the W tile type.

As you can see, it doesn’t go in the south of the state.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Wealthy & Modern Homes
metas.note: Goa and Kerala are two of the most developed states in India and often have very wealthy and modern homes.

metas.name: India - Architecture - West Bengal - Dumka House
metas.note: In West Bengal, houses with walls painted in two colors (green/blue with an orange/brown color at the bottom, are usually found near the Jharkhand border.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Wide W-Tiles
metas.note:
This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.

It is very common in West Bengal, eastern Jharkhand and eastern Bihar, but doesn’t go further north than Purnia, Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Andesite
metas.note: Andesite, a dark, volcanic rock, is a common building material in Bali. You can often see gates, walls, and other intricately carved ornaments built from this material.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Bali Architecture
metas.note: Architecture in Bali is unique because it was influenced by old Balinese culture and Hinduism. The most important thing to look for are these crown-like roof pinnacles, found everywhere in Bali. Guardian statues and slit-drum towers are common too.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Boat Roof - Not Spiky
metas.note:
North Sumatra features similarly distinct boat-shaped roofs, however the roofs are less angled upward and they do not feature spires.

NOTE: These roofs are most commonly found near Lake Toba, due to its sacred history.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Boat Roof - Spiky
metas.note: West Sumatra features these distinct boat-shaped roofs.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Flat Tiles
metas.note: The tiles on roofs in South Kalimantan and Jambi look slightly different. The tiles are usually less rounded but flatter.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Horny Roof
metas.note:
Roofs with gable horns can be found most commonly in South Sulawesi, Riau and Central and South Kalimantan.

NOTE: Horned roofs are often found with Bugis roofs in South Sulawesi. Use this tip along with other clues to determine which region you are in.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Java Roof
metas.note:
Tiled roofs are most commonly found on the island of Java, and sometimes nearby regions such as southern Sumatra, the Lesser Sunda Islands, and South Kalimantan.

NOTE: The tiles on roofs in South Kalimantan and Jambi look slightly different. The tiles are usually less rounded but flatter.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Malay Canopies
metas.note: In the regions of Sumatra and Kalimantan that lie opposite Malaysia, many buildings have metal canopies with curved ends. These canopies are often blue or red.
metas.footer: Source: Real Meta Research Group

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Nias Roof
metas.note: Steeply pitched roofs made of palm tree leaves can sometimes be seen on Nias Island, south west of North Sumatra.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Sheet Roofs
metas.note: Plain sheet metal roofs are more commonly found toward the north, where tiled roofs are not found. They are most commonly found on Kalimantan, Sulawesi and Sumatra.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - South Sula House
metas.note:
These horizontal slots inside the triangles of the roofs are almost unique to Southern Sulawesi.

NOTE: They can rarely be found in East Kalimantan and West Nusa.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Sumba Roof
metas.note: You can find these distinct roofs with uniquely high-pitched peaks on Sumba.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Tongkonan
metas.note: A small region of South Sulawesi, around the city of Rante Pao, features these very unique houses, called Tongkonan, that have saddle-shaped roofs. The houses themselves are also elevated from the ground.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Wooden Chips Roof
metas.note: On Kalimantan, you can find these unique roofs made out of wooden chips.

metas.name: Japan - Architecture - Northern Roofs
metas.note:
The further you are north, roofs generally transition from tiled to level or flat sloped in order to compensate for heavy snowfall. Northern houses often have ladders attached to the side, giving roof access to clear snow.

NOTE: In addition to north to south, high-elevation mountainous regions or high snowfall areas often use such roofs, even in more central or southern prefectures.

metas.name: Japan - Architecture - Okinawa House
metas.note: Okinawa can often be recognised by the white concrete buildings with flat roofs.

metas.name: Japan - Architecture - Red Tiled Roof
metas.note: These unique red-tiled roofs are most commonly found in Chugoku, especially in the prefectures of Hiroshima and Shimane.

metas.name: Japan - Architecture - Shisa
metas.note: You can find these ‘Shisa’ guardian lions and house plaques with these specific characters in Okinawa. The colour and shapes of both can vary.

metas.name: Mexico - Architecture - Mud Brick
metas.note: Mud brick buildings are most abundant in Durango, especially full houses constructed with mud brick. However, they can essentially be found in almost all of the dry desert states.

metas.name: Mexico - Architecture - Northern Mexico Architecture
metas.note: Architecture in northern Mexico often features design elements from American style bungalows. Many houses are coloured with light or pastel colours, gated and commonly have front yards. Orange tiles inspired by Spanish colonial architecture are also typical.

metas.name: Mexico - Architecture - Red Brick
metas.note: Red brick buildings are mostly concentrated in the states west of Mexico City, specifically Jalisco, Michoacan, Guanajuato, and Aguascalientes.

metas.name: Mexico - Architecture - Thatched Roof
metas.note: Thatched roofs are most common in the Yucatan peninsula and eastern San Luis Potosi. They can also be found elsewhere, mainly in the southeast.

metas.name: Mexico - Architecture - White Concrete Blocks
metas.note: White concrete block buildings are highly concentrated in the states surrounding Mexico city, and are generally more common to the east. They can however still be found all over the country.

metas.name: Norway - Architecture - Røros Architecture
metas.note: The old mining town of Røros can be recognised by the densely built traditional wooden architecture.

metas.name: Norway - Architecture - White House Village
metas.note: While completely white wooden houses can be found in the entire country, they're especially common on the southern coast, where you'll commonly see entire villages made up of them.

metas.name: Peru - Architecture - Overhanging Roof
metas.note: Buildings with overhanging roofs with wooden supports are mostly found in northern regions of Peru. These buildings are sometimes brightly coloured as well.

metas.name: Peru - Architecture - Titicaca Architecture
metas.note:
As a general rule, the closer you are to Lake Titicaca in Peru, houses and buildings made out of red brick become more common. This type of architecture resembles the predominant type of building seen in parts of western Bolivia, which is helpful for remembering where it is seen most commonly. Additionally, buildings with blue tinted glass can be seen most commonly in the same areas.

NOTE: Red brick buildings can be seen anywhere in the country, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Philippines - Architecture - Diagonal Amakan
metas.note: Houses built with amakan walls (referred to as Sawali in the north) with a diagonally woven pattern are mostly found on the island of Palawan, but can also be found throughout the northern half of the country.

metas.name: Philippines - Architecture - Diamond Amakan
metas.note: Houses built with amakan walls, a traditionally woven bamboo mat, with a diamond pattern are almost exclusively found in the southern half of the country.

metas.name: Philippines - Architecture - Marawi
metas.note: In and around the city of Marawi, Mindanao you can find many destroyed houses and ruins from the Marawi siege in 2017.

metas.name: Turkey - Architecture - Bodrum Architecture
metas.note: Around the city of Bodrum you will commonly find this type of whitewashed buildings with flat roofs, often combined with blue details or unpainted stone walls.

metas.name: Turkey - Architecture - Flat Roof
metas.note: Flat roofs are mostly found in the southeast and to a lesser extent along the south coast.

metas.name: Turkey - Architecture - Metal Roof
metas.note: Metal roofs are most common in the east.

metas.name: Turkey - Architecture - Pyramid Metal Roof
metas.note: Sheet metal roofs shaped like low pyramids are mainly found far east, particularly in the general area surrounding Lake Van.

metas.name: Turkey - Architecture - Sandstone
metas.note: Many buildings in the Nevşehir Province are built by large, light and unevenly coloured, sandstone bricks.

metas.name: Turkey - Architecture - Tiled Roof
metas.note: Tiled roofs are mostly found in the western two thirds of the country.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Art Deco Architecture
metas.note:
Art Deco is a very distinctive architectural style that is found predominantly in Miami, FL.

There are many features that make it distinct (picture), and a good way to remember them is that they're inspired by ships, for example the Strong central vertical element, which gives the building an appearance like looking straight at a ship. Or round port hole windows, resembling ship windows.

Another distinctive feature is the so-called eyebrows above the windows which have a practical use, which is blocking the strong Miami sunlight from shining into the building and heating it up.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Brick
metas.note: Brick buildings are more common in the Mid-Atlantic states than in other parts of the country. The area around Philadelphia especially has many brick buildings.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Brownstone Architecture
metas.note: ###

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Hank Schrader House
metas.note:
Pueblo Revival style houses are commonly seen in New Mexico. They are typically constructed of adobe or brick and concrete. They have rounded edges and flat roofs, and are usually sand-brown in colour. A famous example for a house like this is the Schrader's residence in Breaking Bad.

NOTE: Pueblo style houses can also be seen in Arizona and Colorado to a lesser extent.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - High Stilts
metas.note: Stilt houses can sometimes be seen on the coast. These are especially common toward the south, and on the Atlantic and Gulf coasts.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Large Sloped Roofs
metas.note: Buildings with very large, sloped roofs are most common in the states of Oklahoma, Texas, and Louisiana. They can also be seen in neighbouring states to a lesser extent.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Miami Modern Architecture
metas.note:
Miami Modern Architecture is characterized by "fun", unconventional designs, decorative elements, smooth corners, flat roofs and lots of glass.

It is find in certain districts of Miami and Miami Beach.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - New Orleans Architecture
metas.note:
Neighbourhoods all around the city of New Orleans feature many colourful, historic, shotgun-style houses.

Buildings in central areas of New Orleans often feature colourful facades with second story wrap-around balconies.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - North-Eastern House
metas.note: Houses in North-Eastern USA often have walls made up of horizontal, overlapping boards

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Red Metal Roof
metas.note:
Buildings with red metal rooftops are most commonly found in the Mid-South and Southern Appalachia states of Virginia, West Virginia, Ohio, Kentucky, Tennessee, Arkansas, and North Carolina.

NOTE: These types of rooftops can be found in other areas, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Shingle Walls
metas.note: Houses in coastal New England often feature shingle walls, which are layered wood panels overlapping each other.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Short Stilt House
metas.note: Houses with short stilts are common in the western and central Gulf Coast. These houses typically feature short stilts made of concrete or wood (30cm-90cm off the ground) and are primarily found in areas near the coast and any adjacent rivers.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Shotgun House
metas.note: Very narrow, one-storey houses made out of wood are called ‘shotgun houses.’ They are most common in and around New Orleans (LA,) Houston (TX,) Louisville (KY,) and the state of Mississippi.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Spanish Colonial Architecture
metas.note:
Spanish Colonial Revival Architecture can be categorised as buildings with lightly-coloured stucco walls and red clay-tile roofs. They can be found in the desert southwest states of California, Nevada, Arizona, and Texas. You can also find similar types of buildings in Florida and coastal Georgia.

Note by MB: See the second picture for an in-depth explanation of this architecture (sorry for the skew, it's a photo I took myself)

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Stacked Triplex
metas.note:
Older three story wooden houses, also called ‘stacked triplexes,’ are very common in urban areas of the Northeast. They are most prevalent in New York, Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts.

NOTE: These types of houses are also somewhat common in cities in Atlantic Canada.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Trailer House
metas.note: Small, rectangular manufactured homes, also known as mobile or ‘trailer’ homes, are popular in rural areas of the US. In general, mobile homes are more common in the Southeast but they can be seen anywhere in the country.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Victorian Architecture
metas.note: Row Houses and other buildings in San Francisco are often in the style of Victorian architecture, with many bay windows, turrets, and ornate exterior details. These homes are built close together and can be very colourful.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Wooden House
metas.note: Houses and commercial buildings in the interior Western US are often made of lots of dark wooden boards and timbers. Buildings at high elevations also commonly have metal roofs, to avoid snow build-up.
